bodyHtml:
How long does a root-canalled tooth last?

Many root-canalled teeth last for years, and often for a lifetime, when they are properly restored and cared for. There is no fixed expiry date: longevity depends on the tooth, the quality of the final restoration, your oral hygiene, and factors such as grinding or further decay. What research consistently shows is that a well-treated and well-restored tooth has a good long-term outlook, though no dentist can promise a specific number of years.

It helps to think of a root canal as saving the tooth, and the restoration that follows as protecting that investment. The two work together.

What the evidence generally shows

Large studies of root canal (endodontic) treatment report high survival rates over many years, with the majority of treated teeth still functioning well long after treatment. Professional bodies such as the American Association of Endodontists describe root canal therapy as a predictable way to keep a natural tooth that would otherwise be lost. Keeping your own tooth also helps preserve the surrounding bone and your natural bite in a way that even good replacements cannot fully copy.

That said, averages are not guarantees. Some teeth need further treatment, and a small number are eventually lost. The goal of the information below is to show you which factors you and your dental team can influence, so the outlook is not simply a matter of luck. In practice, two people can have the same root canal and very different long-term results depending on how the tooth is restored and looked after afterwards.

What affects how long a treated tooth lasts

The final restoration

This is one of the biggest factors. A root-treated tooth that receives a timely, well-sealed filling or crown tends to do far better than one left under a temporary restoration or never properly rebuilt. Back teeth in particular often need a crown to guard against fracture.

The tooth and the original problem

Front teeth with simple anatomy and modest damage are generally straightforward. Molars with several canals, or teeth that were badly broken down or cracked before treatment, can be more demanding and may carry a slightly different outlook.

Your daily care

A root-canalled tooth can still get decay at its margins, because the outer tooth is still exposed to bacteria. Brushing, cleaning between teeth, and regular check-ups all protect the result. Night-time grinding (bruxism) can stress the tooth, and a night guard may be suggested if that applies to you.

Timely follow-up

Completing the recommended restoration promptly, and returning for reviews, lets your dentist catch small problems early — before they threaten the tooth.

Signs to keep an eye on

A successfully treated tooth is usually comfortable and simply blends into normal function. Reasons to check in with your dentist include new or returning pain, tenderness when biting, swelling, or a bump on the gum near the tooth. These do not always mean the tooth is failing, but they are worth assessing. In some cases, root canal therapy at Smile Dental Arts Centre can be reviewed and, if needed, other options discussed.

Can a root canal tooth last forever?

Some do effectively last the rest of a person's life, but "forever" is not something any dentist can promise. Good restoration and good home care give the tooth its best chance.

Does a crown make it last longer?

For many back teeth, yes — full-coverage protection reduces the risk of fracture, which is a leading reason treated teeth are lost. Your dentist will advise whether your tooth needs one.

Can a root canal tooth get a cavity again?

Yes. The treated tooth no longer feels pain in the usual way, but its outer surfaces can still develop decay like any other tooth. That is why ongoing brushing, cleaning between teeth, and regular check-ups remain just as important after a root canal as before.

Protecting your result

The practical takeaway is encouraging: much of what determines a root-canalled tooth's lifespan is within reach. Complete the recommended restoration, keep up daily cleaning, manage grinding if it affects you, and attend regular reviews. Dr. Neda Kadivar, a general and family dentist with over 20 years of experience, provides root canal treatment at Smile Dental Arts Centre in Markham, Ontario, where you can ask about caring for a treated tooth over the long term.

This article is general information and not a substitute for professional dental advice, diagnosis, or treatment. Always speak with a licensed dentist about your specific situation.
